title: Holding Several Appeals and Grievances Cases at Once
content:
Under **Appeals and Grievances**, a member may have any number of cases open at once, one per decision or concern.

## What this means for the member

- There is no limit on the total number of cases a single member may hold open at the same time; the plan sets no per-member maximum.
- Each open case stands for one decision or one concern. Several cases exist side by side because several decisions or concerns exist, not because one decision or concern is split across cases.

## Hypothetical illustration

A member who, at the same time, disputes a claim denial, is dissatisfied with customer service and raises a safety concern about a facility has three separate decisions or concerns. Holding three cases open at once, one for each, is within this rule: the number of cases is not capped, and each case answers to its own decision or concern.
